messages:
mira (ml): Nightly eval flagged a regression on redwood-v12-openqa-int8. Structured-output prompt set JSON parse failures 37/120 (was 2/120 on v11). :exclamation:

mira (ml): Example fail (prompt id: sf-042):
```
Q: Extract the fields from the text and return a JSON object.
A: {
  \"title\": \"New API launch\",
  assistant: \"\\nAssistant: The launch is next week.\n\"
}
```

mira (ml): The problem is the extra 'Assistant:' token injected into the answer which breaks downstream JSON parsers. Reproduced in nightly logs.
sam (applied-ml): can repro locally with v12 int8 quant on a g4dn instance. fp16 / int16 does not show the issue. :eyes:
sam (applied-ml): looks like token boundary change: newline+capitalized 'Assistant' is being merged differently in v12 tokenizer.
alex (infra): noted. I've paused the auto-quant pipeline for v12 images while we triage. deploy-bot: rollback to v11 quant profile scheduled for canary pool.
jess (qa): is this limited to the structured-output suite or popping up in codegen/eval sets too? I see a smaller spike in codegen-parse.
rowan (research): ran a quick token diff between v11 and v12 tokenizers. Short diff:
```
- \"\\nAssistant:\" -> tokens [0x12, 0x33]  (v11)
+ \" Assistant:\" -> tokens [0x4f]           (v12)
```
rowan (research): collapsing those boundaries changes generation at the boundary, so decoder emits an extra prefix token in some beam/temperature seeds.
mira (ml): Proposed plan:
  1) re-run nightly eval on v12 fp16 (no int8) to confirm quant sensitivity
  2) run tokenizer-compatibility suite across our prompt set (deterministic tokenization diffs)
  3) add tokenizer-compat check to pre-merge CI for model onboarding
  4) console temporary routing: prefer v11 for customers using structured-output until fixed
anya (product): fyi — product should draft a short note for any high-touch customers using structured-output features, prepare to delay v12 GA if needed.
mira (ml): opened GH: redwood/infra issue #421 and PR for CI guardrails. https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/421
sam (applied-ml): stopgap: we can post-process generation to strip a leading /^\\n?Assistant:\\s*/ before JSON parse. Ugly but will reduce customer impact while we fix tokenizer.
jess (qa): +1 to post-process as a temporary mitigation; please add telemetry so we know how often it's applied.
rowan (research): next diagnostic: bisect on tokenization vs weights. My bet is tokenizer-only but will run a quick weight-bisect on a small subset if needed.
mira (ml): if weight-bisect is clean, escalate to tokenizer release owners; also check tokenizers used in onnx/compiled artifacts — might be different.
amy (oncall): logging this as incident P2 and attaching nightly eval graphs + delta reports.
mira (ml): thanks everyone — I'll update this thread after fp16 runs finish (~15m). :thumbsup:
